title: Footwear and grip
audience: Trainee or new worker on the window cleaning (all heights) track, working under supervision.
learningOutcomes: Inspect enclosed slip-resistant footwear for worn tread, trapped debris, damage and contamination before each shift.
Explain why footwear reduces slip risk but does not replace barriers, dry routes or prompt spill management.
Identify footwear that no longer gives adequate support or traction and report site footwear rules that conflict with safe work.

instruction.heading: Exterior, height and access context
instruction.body: This lesson is part of the window cleaning (all heights) track. The track covers ground-level, water-fed pole and elevated access work on glazing and frames. Any work above ground level, or from a ladder, scaffold or elevating work platform, is restricted: it needs employer authorisation under a site-specific risk assessment, and the worker must hold any licence the relevant state or territory requires for the equipment used. This lesson does not grant the right to work at height or on solar systems.

instruction.heading: Overview
instruction.body: This lesson develops practical competence in footwear and grip for routine professional cleaning work. Apply the employer’s site procedures and stop if a task falls outside your training or authority.

instruction.heading: Instruction
instruction.body: Inspect enclosed slip-resistant footwear for wear, contamination and suitability; change footwear where site hygiene requires it.

instruction.heading: Prepare and verify
instruction.body: Choose enclosed footwear suitable for the floor conditions, task and site rules. Inspect soles for worn tread, trapped debris, damage and contamination before each shift.

instruction.heading: Perform the work safely and professionally
instruction.body: Wet floors, grease, polished surfaces and stairs create different slip risks. Footwear reduces risk but does not replace barriers, dry routes, controlled work zones or prompt spill management.

instruction.heading: Check, record and escalate
instruction.body: Clean and dry footwear appropriately after work; replace footwear that no longer provides adequate support or traction. Report site footwear rules that conflict with safe task performance.

instruction.heading: Stop-work rule
instruction.body: Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

procedure: Choose enclosed footwear suited to the floor conditions, the task and the site rules.
Inspect the soles for worn tread, trapped debris, damage and contamination before each shift.
Replace any footwear that no longer gives adequate support or traction.
Use barriers, dry routes and controlled work zones, since footwear alone does not control slip risk.
Manage spills promptly and keep wet floors controlled.
Clean and dry footwear after work, as the site requires.
Report any site footwear rule that conflicts with safe task performance.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Licence and height notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work at height, on roofs, from elevated work platforms, or on solar systems. Completing it is not a licence, certificate or authority for regulated work. Boom-type elevating work platforms need a high risk work licence in Victoria at any boom length, and in New South Wales, Queensland, Tasmania, the Northern Territory and Western Australia where the boom is 11 metres or more. The WorkSafe WA page (last updated 13 August 2026) and the NT WorkSafe bulletin (no date shown) both state the 11-metre threshold. Check whether this work needs a high-risk work licence with the state regulator before you start. Queensland's definition does not cover platforms under 11 metres (WorkSafe Queensland page, no date shown). Tasmania's WP licence applies where the boom length is 11 metres or more, and no licence is needed for a boom under 11 metres (WorkSafe Tasmania page, last updated 1 December 2023). In New South Wales and Queensland the boom length is 11 metres: a boom-type platform of 11 metres or more needs the licence, and a shorter boom may not need it in those states. Victoria's WP class has no boom-length threshold, so the licence is not limited by length there. This lesson does not grant a licence. Scissor lifts need no high risk work licence in Victoria or the Northern Territory. Check the licence rules for your state or territory and obtain your employer's written authorisation before any work above ground level.

Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

qualityStandard: Enclosed footwear suited to the floor conditions and task is chosen.
Soles are inspected for worn tread, trapped debris, damage and contamination before each shift.
Footwear is not treated as a substitute for barriers, dry routes or spill management.
Footwear without adequate support or traction is replaced, and conflicting site footwear rules are reported.
summary: Enclosed slip-resistant footwear is inspected for worn tread, trapped debris, damage and contamination before each shift.
Footwear reduces slip risk but does not replace barriers, dry routes or prompt spill management.
Footwear that no longer gives adequate support or traction is replaced, and site footwear rules that conflict with safe work are reported.

knowledgeChecks.question: What should you do if your footwear does not suit a wet-floor task?
options: Stop and tell the supervisor before going further
Wear open shoes if the site allows it
Rely on your footwear to make the task safe
Continue because other crews on site are doing the same task

knowledgeChecks.question: How should a site footwear rule that conflicts with safe work be handed over?
options: Tell the supervisor the rule conflicts with safe performance, and say what the risk is
Work around the rule and sort it out at home and tell the supervisor later
Leave it to the next worker and say nothing about it to anyone on the site at all
Keep quiet about the rule to avoid a fuss and work around it until the job ends

knowledgeChecks.question: Which footwear is correct for the floor conditions on a wet-floor job?
options: Slippers, since they are quiet on floors and they are comfortable to wear
Sandals, since they are cooler and they dry fast on wet floors
Flat-soled canvas shoes, chosen for comfort over grip today
Enclosed slip-resistant footwear suited to the floor conditions and task

knowledgeChecks.question: Which footwear practice is unsafe on a wet walkway?
options: Replacing footwear once the tread is worn and the sole is checked every week
Cleaning and drying footwear after work and keeping spare pairs in the van
Using a dry route through the work area and marking the route with signs
Relying on footwear alone on a wet walkway, with no barrier or drying

knowledgeChecks.question: What should be recorded and escalated about worn footwear?
options: Nothing needs recording for footwear if the supervisor has already seen it
Keep worn footwear until the next scheduled audit and wear it on the next site as well
Record and escalate worn footwear and any site footwear rule that conflicts with safe work
Post a photo of the footwear to a personal group chat with the site name and the time
